Farooq, L. Zafar, K. Rehman Department of Environmental Sciences, University of Karachi. DOI: 10.1016/j.jwpe.2024.105210 Abstract Polyethersulfone (PES) membranes containing 0 to 1.5 wt% ZIF-67 were prepared by non-solvent induced phase separation and tested for dye removal in cross-flow mode. The membrane containing 1.0 wt% ZIF-67 reached 187 LMH and rejected 95.6% of methylene blue. Published: 2 June 2024. 1. Introduction Dyeing and finishing operations in the textile sector release large volumes of coloured effluent that is toxic to aquatic life and difficult to treat biologically. Nanofiltration and loose ultrafiltration are attractive because they can retain dyes while allowing salts to pass, but flux decline caused by fouling limits their application. Several mixed-matrix designs have been reported. Zhang et al. described a PES membrane with graphene oxide that reached a rejection of 99% for Congo red at 6 bar, whereas Ali and co-workers obtained a flux of 210 LMH with a TiO2 filler but only 82% methylene blue retention.
